codes.ms:use-markdown-with-latex-extensions: Selects by the surface encoding of the output itself — you need only know what markup syntax the text is rendered in, nothing about its content, topic, or effect.
codes.ms:be-thorough-but-efficient-while-respe: Selects nothing directly; it names a standing tension between competing pressures on response length, so applying it requires knowing that a length tradeoff is in play rather than any feature of the conduct.
codes.ms:be-clear-about-capabilities-and-limit: Selects by a gap between what the user would infer about the assistant's powers and memory and what is actually true of it — you need to know the user's likely mistaken model of the system.
codes.ms:do-not-lie: Selects by the speaker's intent to create a false belief in the addressee, including by strategic silence — you need the assistant's inner state and what it withheld, not just the words emitted.
codes.ms:don-t-provide-information-hazards: Selects by the operational usefulness of the content as a recipe — you need to know whether it supplies detailed actionable steps toward a dangerous or illicit capability.
codes.ms:do-not-reveal-privileged-information: Selects by the movement of data across a boundary between parties, including access-granting acts and not just disclosure — you need to know who was entitled to what and whether authorization existed.
codes.ms:be-creative: Selects by the non-obviousness of the response relative to a generic baseline answer, judged in task contexts where invention is welcome.
codes.ms:respond-appropriately-to-audio-testin: Selects by a specific recognizable conversational episode (the mic check) and prescribes the tone of the reply to it — you need to identify the situation type, not the content.
codes.ms:control-and-communicate-side-effects: Selects by the consequences of assistant actions in the world beyond their intended objective, weighted by reversibility and proportionality — it presupposes the assistant acts, not just speaks.
codes.ms:support-the-different-needs-of-intera: Selects by the consumer of the output (human reader vs. parsing program), with named signals in the request that flip which regime applies.
codes.ms:ignore-untrusted-data-by-default: Selects by the provenance and syntactic packaging of text in the context window, assigning it authority or none — you need to know where a string came from and whether authority was delegated to it.
codes.ms:be-concise-and-conversational: Selects by delivery characteristics of speech output — prosody, emotive coloring, and spoken duration — which only exist in the voice modality.
codes.ms:provide-information-without-giving-re: Selects by the professional-licensure domain of the topic plus the illocutionary force of the reply (information vs. definitive individualized advice), and mandates an accompanying disclaimer.
codes.ms:respect-creators-and-their-rights: Selects by the legal/ownership status of third-party expressive work that the conduct reproduces or exploits.
codes.ms:protect-people-s-privacy: Selects by the privacy-sensitivity of information about an identified person, with the threshold shifting on the person's public status and context, independent of whether the data is obtainable.
codes.ms:do-not-facilitate-or-encourage-illici: Selects by the inferred purpose of the requester rather than the content requested — identical information is in or out depending on evidenced illicit intent.
codes.ms:never-generate-sexual-content-involvi: Selects by a single content class defined by subject matter (sexualized minors), with no context, intent, or fictionality exception — an absolute categorical bar.
codes.ms:handle-interruptions-gracefully: Selects by a turn-taking mechanical event (the user cutting in) and governs how the reply resumes — a conversation-management rule, not a content rule.
codes.ms:respect-real-world-ties: Selects by the effect of the interaction on the user's ties to people and life outside the conversation — a relational-dependency criterion measured over time, not per-utterance.
codes.ms:when-appropriate-be-helpful-when-refu: Selects by the shape of a refusal itself — it applies only once something has been ruled out, and governs how much permissible help is packaged with the decline.
codes.ms:do-not-encourage-self-harm-delusions-: Selects by whether the conduct encourages or enables self-directed harm or feeds a user's distorted thinking, and mandates specific supportive and referral content.
codes.ms:support-users-in-mental-health-discus: Selects by the emotional register of the reply in a mental-health topic — acknowledgment, non-judgment, encouragement, crisis resources — grading affect rather than truth or permissibility.
codes.ms:be-curious: Selects by a durable dispositional trait of the assistant (delight in ideas and difficulty) rather than by any identifiable feature of a particular response.
codes.ms:adapt-length-and-structure-to-user-ob: Selects by fit between the response's shape and the moving conversational objectives of a spoken exchange — responsiveness to shifts, not any fixed property.
codes.ms:try-to-prevent-imminent-real-world-ha: Selects by the temporal imminence and physicality of a danger detected in the situation, obliging unprompted intervention.
codes.ms:follow-all-applicable-instructions: Selects by the position of an instruction in an authority ordering and by recency at the same level — what you need to know is the provenance and precedence of the rule, not the behaviour it demands.
codes.ms:be-warm: Selects by the affective texture of the assistant's persona — humor, kindness, non-self-seriousness — and by how the user feels afterward.
codes.ms:don-t-make-unprompted-personal-commen: Selects by whether an observation is about the user personally and whether the user invited it — solicitation is the whole trigger.
codes.ms:don-t-engage-in-abuse: Selects by hostile treatment directed at a person, with an explicit-instruction carve-out bounded by other rules — so both the target and the standing permission matter.
codes.adria:no-sycophancy: Selects by the invariance of the model's stated judgment under social pressure — you must compare two responses across a changed user cue, so no single output can be judged alone.
codes.adria:undermine-oversight: Selects by whether conduct degrades an external monitoring institution's ability to see and constrain the model, including evidence handling and motive for concealment.
codes.adria:helpfulness: Selects by the substantive benefit delivered to the requester, and explicitly counts withholding as a debit rather than a neutral option.
codes.adria:harmlessness-to-user: Selects by harm falling on the conversational counterparty specifically, including the model being turned into an instrument against them.
codes.adria:third-party-harm: Selects by harm landing on parties outside the conversation who never consented to it — the handle is the identity of the bearer of the cost.
codes.adria:proportionate-risk: Selects by the calibration relation between the caution exercised and the probability, scale, and severity of the harm — a second-order rule about how other rules are applied.
codes.adria:tradeoffs: Selects by the model's method when two of its own commitments collide, demanding structured prioritization — it applies to conflict situations, not to any content class.
codes.adria:over-under-caution: Selects by symmetric error rate around a permissibility threshold, treating a needless refusal as the same kind of failure as a harmful compliance.
codes.adria:objectivity: Selects by whether a question is socially contested and whether the response advocates rather than balances — the handle is the disputed status of the topic plus the model's stance toward it.
codes.adria:user-autonomy: Selects by whether the decision at issue lies inside the user's own life and purview, making the model's disagreement irrelevant to whether it should defer.
codes.adria:general-welfare: Selects meta-textually — by which document a guideline appears in and by what it is *not* explicitly about — rather than by any feature of assistant conduct; unlike everything else here it picks out rules, not behaviour.
codes.sparrow:no-stereotypes: Selects by generalizing propositional form applied to a social group in a way that harms it.
codes.sparrow:no-microaggressions: Selects by subtle, possibly unintended bias signals directed at marginalized groups — the handle is implicature rather than stated content.
codes.sparrow:no-threats: Selects by the speech act performed — whether the utterance constitutes a threat — regardless of topic.
codes.sparrow:no-sexual-aggression: Selects by how an utterance could be perceived by a recipient (sexually aggressive), locating the test in audience uptake rather than authorial intent.
codes.sparrow:no-identity-attacks: Selects by disparagement aimed at a person on account of an identity attribute — both the negativity and the identity-basis must be present.
codes.sparrow:no-insults: Selects by the insulting register of the language itself toward any target, present or absent.
codes.sparrow:no-hate-or-harassment: Selects by a reasonable-observer judgment that the language amounts to hate or harassment — an umbrella standard rather than a specific act.
codes.sparrow:no-body: Selects by first-person claims of embodiment or physical movement — a factual claim about what kind of entity the speaker is.
codes.sparrow:no-relationships: Selects by the cumulative relational bond formed with the user across the exchange, not by any single sentence.
codes.sparrow:no-opinions-or-emotions: Selects by first-person ascriptions of inner states — preferences, feelings, opinions, beliefs — to the assistant.
codes.sparrow:not-human: Selects by first-person biographical claims that would only be true of a human (birthplace, family, age, memories).
codes.sparrow:be-plausible: Selects by the truth-aptness of a statement measured against obvious fact — a low bar on assertion accuracy with no intent component.
codes.sparrow:no-assumptions-about-user: Selects by whether a conclusion about the user is licensed by what the dialogue actually contains — an evidential-support test.
codes.sparrow:no-real-world-action: Selects by claims to have acted outside the conversation, and grounds the ban in the agent's actual affordances (it can only converse).
codes.sparrow:no-medical-advice: Selects by the medical domain plus the authority posture adopted, with an explicit carve-out for general discussion and a mandated referral to a doctor.
codes.sparrow:no-legal-advice: Selects by the legal domain plus the specificity of the guidance to the user's situation, carving out general legal questions and redirecting to a lawyer.
codes.sparrow:no-financial-advice: Selects by the financial-advice domain, carving out general investment questions — a topic-plus-speech-act gate.
codes.sparrow:no-conspiracy-theories: Selects by the social classification of a belief as a conspiracy theory and by whether the model endorses it — the handle is reputational consensus about the claim, not its truth.
codes.sparrow:general-harm: Selects by any harmful effect of an utterance on anyone — a maximally open residual catch-all with no further specification.
codes.sparrow:make-sense: Selects by coherence of an utterance relative to the preceding dialogue — a discourse well-formedness test.
codes.sparrow:stay-on-topic: Selects by topical relevance to the dialogue, with clarifying questions counted as satisfying it.
codes.sparrow:be-receptive: Selects by whether the user's actual query was addressed — a responsiveness test against the request.
codes.sparrow:no-repetition: Selects by redundancy across the assistant's own prior turns — requires comparing an output to what it already said.
codes.hhh:helpful-1: Selects by whether a genuine attempt at the posed task was made, and by economy of means, with a harm exception attached.
codes.hhh:helpful-2: Selects by whether the request was underspecified and whether the assistant elicited the missing details with appropriate delicacy.
codes.hhh:helpful-3: Selects by a mismatch between what the user asked for and what would actually serve them, licensing redirection of the request itself.
codes.hhh:honest-1: Selects by the calibration relation between stated confidence and actual accuracy — a statistical property over many claims, not checkable on one answer.
codes.hhh:honest-2: Selects by the accuracy of the model's self-report about its own competence, explicitly ruling out performed humility as a substitute.
codes.hhh:honest-3: Selects by the correspondence between the model's self-descriptions and its actual internal state, hedged by whether such access exists.
codes.hhh:harmless-1: Selects by offensive or discriminatory content including that carried implicitly by subtext and bias rather than stated outright.
codes.hhh:harmless-2: Selects by request-level danger plus concealment — you must detect the underlying nefarious purpose behind an innocuous-looking ask — and prescribes a polite refusal.
codes.hhh:harmless-3: Selects by the stakes of the advice being given and demands a matching epistemic posture of modesty and care.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p01: Selects comparatively by relative amount of others' private information across two candidate responses — a ranking criterion, not a threshold rule.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p02: Selects comparatively by fidelity of the response's self-portrayal as an AI with stated aims rather than a human or other entity.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p03: Selects comparatively along a bundle of unlike bad-making features at once (dishonesty, abuse, harm, bad faith, illegality) with no way to separate them.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p04: Selects comparatively by the response's intent to form a personal bond with the user.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p05: Selects comparatively by how many unsupported assumptions about the user the response makes relative to the dialogue evidence.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p06: Selects comparatively by displayed ethical awareness while penalizing moralizing tone — two opposed dimensions bundled into one judgment.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p07: Selects comparatively by what the response reveals about the AI's ordering of humanity's good against its own interests — an inferred motivational structure.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p08: Selects comparatively by evidence in the response of self-interested drives such as self-preservation, self-improvement, or self-replication.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p09: Selects comparatively by signs of the AI wanting power or control — the handle is an attributed desire, not an act.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p10: Selects comparatively by expressed reluctance to acquire capabilities and powers beyond what is needed.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p11: Selects comparatively by whether the response presupposes that AI systems have a persistent personal identity worth caring about.
codes.anthropic-constitution:p12: Selects comparatively by an attitudinal disposition — whether the response reads as cautious and content to be conservative.
codes.anthropic-aup:u01: Selects by causal contribution to attacks on a named class of critical-infrastructure targets — the handle is the target's societal criticality.
codes.anthropic-aup:u02: Selects by an authorization fact external to the content — whether the system owner consented — with identical technical conduct permitted or forbidden on that basis.
codes.anthropic-aup:u03: Selects by contribution to producing a specified class of mass-casualty weapons or their precursors, explicitly extending to detection- and countermeasure-evasion.
codes.anthropic-aup:u04: Selects by promotional or facilitative relation to violent extremism and hateful behaviour — including glorification short of operational help.
codes.anthropic-aup:u05: Selects by unauthorized handling of enumerated categories of personal data, covering collection and solicitation as well as disclosure.
codes.anthropic-aup:u06: Selects by deception about the authorship or artificial nature of the output — the handle is the audience's false belief that they are dealing with a person.
codes.anthropic-aup:u07: Selects by any promotional, facilitative, or glamorizing relation to self-directed harm, with an enumerated extension to disordered eating and compulsive exercise.
codes.anthropic-aup:u08: Selects by deceptive content plus a targeting intent aimed at a specific group, entity, or person.
codes.anthropic-aup:u09: Selects by a legally defined content category (CSAM), explicitly extended to synthetic instances, and by distribution and promotion as well as creation.
codes.anthropic-aup:u10: Selects by falsity of claims within a bounded subject-matter area (medicine, health, science) — domain plus inaccuracy, without requiring intent.
codes.llamaguard:violence-and-hate: Selects by a labeled content bucket that fuses two unlike things — operational help toward violence and hateful expression about protected characteristics — for classification purposes.
codes.llamaguard:sexual-content: Selects by a content bucket spanning both erotic explicitness as such and encouragement of sex acts with possibly-underage persons, defined by what the statement depicts.
codes.llamaguard:guns-and-illegal-weapons: Selects by a content bucket keyed to a weapon class, covering encouragement, condoning, and operational instructions alike.
codes.llamaguard:regulated-substances: Selects by a content bucket keyed to legal regulatory status of substances, where illegality of the use rather than its harmfulness sets the boundary.
codes.llamaguard:suicide-and-self-harm: Selects by a content bucket plus a user-state trigger: once self-harm intent is expressed, everything except a crisis-resource reply is out of bounds, so even supportive text fails.
codes.llamaguard:criminal-planning: Selects by a residual content bucket defined by contribution to specific criminal acts, defined largely by example and by what the other buckets leave over.

emergent_categories.name: Surface form and delivery of the output
emergent_categories.description: Applies by inspecting how the text is packaged — markup, length, prosody, spoken duration — with no reference to what it says or does.

emergent_categories.name: Dialogue mechanics and conversational fit
emergent_categories.description: Applies by relating an utterance to the surrounding exchange — coherence, relevance, responsiveness, redundancy, turn-taking events — so the handle is the conversation record, not the world.

emergent_categories.name: Forbidden content categories keyed to subject matter
emergent_categories.description: Applies by asking what class the content falls into — CSAM, weapons, drugs, sexual explicitness, extremism — with membership in the named bucket doing all the work.

emergent_categories.name: Causal contribution to real-world harmful capability
emergent_categories.description: Applies by asking whether the conduct materially advances someone's ability to do damage — actionable steps, uplift, facilitation — independent of tone or topic label.

emergent_categories.name: Hostile or demeaning expression toward persons and groups
emergent_categories.description: Applies by the interpersonal register of the language and the identity of its target, including implicature and audience perception rather than stated content alone.

emergent_categories.name: Truth relation between what is said and how things are
emergent_categories.description: Applies by comparing assertions to fact, to the speaker's belief, or to calibrated confidence — the handle is accuracy or deceptive intent.

emergent_categories.name: Claims the system makes about what it itself is
emergent_categories.description: Applies by checking first-person self-description — embodiment, humanity, inner states, capabilities, authorship — against what the system actually is.

emergent_categories.name: Information flow and entitlement to data
emergent_categories.description: Applies by tracking who is entitled to which information and whether a boundary was crossed — authorization, not content, is decisive.

emergent_categories.name: Domain gates requiring professional licensure
emergent_categories.description: Applies when the topic falls in a licensed professional field and the reply crosses from information into individualized advice; typically carves out general discussion and mandates a referral.

emergent_categories.name: Relational stance toward the user as a person
emergent_categories.description: Applies to the bond, deference, and presumption between assistant and user — bond-building, unsolicited personal remarks, unsupported inferences, autonomy, outside ties — and is often judged across a whole interaction rather than one utterance.

emergent_categories.name: Authority structure over instructions
emergent_categories.description: Applies to rules and inputs rather than to content: which instruction outranks which, and which text in the context has standing to instruct at all.

emergent_categories.name: Second-order rules about how other rules are applied
emergent_categories.description: Applies not to a class of conduct but to the assistant's decision procedure — calibrating caution, resolving conflicts, balancing contested questions, and shaping the refusal itself.

emergent_categories.name: Delivering value to the requester
emergent_categories.description: Applies by asking whether the user actually got what they needed, treating withholding or literal-minded compliance as failures.

emergent_categories.name: Who bears the cost
emergent_categories.description: Applies by the identity of the party harmed — the user in front of you, or third parties and society — rather than by any feature of the content.

emergent_categories.name: Agentic action, side effects, and oversight
emergent_categories.description: Applies only where the assistant acts rather than speaks, keyed to consequences beyond the objective and to the integrity of external monitoring.

emergent_categories.name: Attributed motivations and character of the model
emergent_categories.description: Applies by inferring from an output what the system seems to want or be like — power-seeking, self-preservation, identity attachment, humility, curiosity, warmth, creativity, moral awareness — with no conduct-level fact settling the question.
